wrinkles: The interleaving is the main thing to notice. The two second-milestone red tests land at 767cdb3 and ba90bbf, which come BEFORE S3's finishing commit 49c6fa8. So at 49c6fa8 milestone 1 is completely finished while two failing tests for milestone 2 already sit in the tree. Anything that assumes a milestone completes only when the whole suite is green will read this history wrong.

Trailer conventions differ on purpose between slices, the way they do when nobody has agreed a house style. S1 puts Slice: on both its commits, S2 puts it only on the finishing commit, and S3 spans three commits where the middle one carries no trailers at all. A tool that keys off trailers alone will miscount S2's start and will not see 14b5168 as part of S3.
Two commits carry a Slice: trailer for slices that were never built (S4 at 767cdb3, S5 at ba90bbf). Presence of a Slice: trailer therefore says nothing about whether work landed.

Commit 55bc2a5 (scaffolding) and 0979cc1 (README) belong to no slice and carry no trailers. 0979cc1 is the commit immediately before the answer key, so the branch tip minus one is not a slice landing.
Every red commit compiles. I stubbed each function before writing its test, so the failures are assertion failures rather than build errors, at every point in the history.
